mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met, or the effect reverses for more than two consecutive tightening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the relationship inverts during three consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals persistent labor market slack, which reduces wage growth and corporate margin potential, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: post-recession recovery or weak labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered periods, or the effect disappears for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of 1% or more, coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) of less than 0.5%, indicates a supply-side contraction without offsetting housing demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% AND HOUST monthly change < 0.5%
regime_hint: manufacturing downturn with weak housing momentum
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the effect is not statistically significant at p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in CPIAUCSL above 4% while FEDFUNDS remains below 2% signals unmet inflation expectations, prompting anticipation of future rate hikes and higher discount rates, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 4% AND FEDFUNDS < 2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered months, or the effect is not robust during two consecutive inflation surprise episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A positive year-over-year change in real personal savings (RSAFS) exceeding 5% combined with a flat or declining GDP (GDPC1) suggests households are saving more due to precautionary motives, reducing consumption and investment, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS YoY change > 5% AND GDPC1 YoY change <= 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered quarters, or the relationship inverts for three consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of less than 50,000 while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) simultaneously rises signals weak labor market momentum, which reduces earnings growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change < 50,000 AND UNRATE monthly change > 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered months, or the effect is not significant at p < 0.10 for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) of more than 10% for four consecutive months signals a deepening housing downturn, which reduces construction-related economic activity and drags on corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered periods, or the effect is not statistically significant over any five-year rolling window.
